title: The Crucial Role of Semiconductors in the Software-Defined Vehicle
problem: Modern vehicles require software-defined architectures to meet emission standards, enable intelligent connectivity, and support sustainable mobility—demanding advanced semiconductor solutions.
motivation: Regulatory pressure on emissions, consumer demand for smart/connected vehicles, and sustainability goals are driving the automotive industry toward software-defined vehicle (SDV) platforms.
method: Position paper outlining the semiconductor technology roadmap and system requirements to enable software-defined vehicle architectures with central compute, over-the-air updates, and intelligent edge processing.
key_novelty: Framing semiconductors as foundational enabler for automotive software-defined transformation.
contributions: Articulation of semiconductor requirements for software-defined vehicles
Connection between chip design and automotive system architecture
Industry transformation perspective on SDV technology drivers
